subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: If α, β, 1 are the roots of x³ − 2x² − 5x + 6 = 0, then find α and β.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Senior Inter Maths-2A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.76 — VSAQ chapter 15 Theory of Equations, answer 131. Printed appearances: AP 16 · TS 17. ⚠ THE 1+1 SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — the VSAQ chapter (book pp.76–77) prints no [N Marks] tags. It is the 1+1 this publisher prints for a 2-mark VSAQ in its Maths-1A volume (Matrices, book p.82 there): one mark for the relation or substitution that sets the question up, one for the value. The SAME step ids (s1_relation, s2_answer) are used on answers 127, 128, 130 and 131, deliberately: one root relation (S₁ = −a₁/a₀ or S₃ = −a₃/a₀) read off the coefficients, then one line of arithmetic. The book's chapter header carries ★★★; that star is the CHAPTER's rank, not this question's. Paper position: Maths-2A Section A runs Q1–Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory; Q5 is the Theory of Equations slot (blueprint, book p.3; all five model papers pp.111–120 agree). Model Paper 4 Q5 (book p.117) is this question; the Bullet Model Paper re-solves it under Q5 on book p.97. CORRECTION TO THE BOOK, recorded not silently fixed: the book prints the equation as x³ − 2x² + 5x + 6 = 0 (book p.76 answer 131, the Bullet Model Paper Q5 block on p.97, and Model Paper 4 Q5 on p.117 — the same misprint in all three places). For that equation 1 is NOT a root: f(1) = 1 − 2 + 5 + 6 = 10 ≠ 0, so the question as printed has no answer, and the book's own working (α + β = 1, αβ = −6, so 3 and −2) does not satisfy it either (3 · (−2) + 3 + (−2) = −5 ≠ +5 = a₂/a₀). The Telugu Akademi textbook question (Exercise 4(a)) reads x³ − 2x² − 5x + 6 = 0, for which 1 is a root (1 − 2 − 5 + 6 = 0) and the book's answer α = 3, β = −2 is exactly right. The card is authored with the −5x equation; the answer 3, −2 is unchanged. Truth check: (x − 1)(x − 3)(x + 2) = x³ − 2x² − 5x + 6. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. No two-book check and no board back-test exist for this paper (no second Maths-2A source in the corpus; answer-book/papers/ holds first-year physics only) — recorded, not hidden. A back-test against the book's own six papers (the five Model Guess Papers plus the Bullet Model Paper, 199 slot-instances) WAS run on 2026-08-29: all 199 resolved to an authored card, and every one carried the section and marks its slot implies. That is a substitute corpus, not a board paper — it cannot show what the board asks that this book omits.

recall_prompt: Say which two relations you would use, what each gives, and how you get the two roots from them.
insider_note: The book prints +5x in three places; 1 is not a root of that equation, and the textbook's −5x is the one whose roots are 3 and −2.

steps.label: Sum and product
steps.margin_note: First mark. Two unknown roots need two relations. The sum gives α + β and the product gives αβ, because the third root is 1.
steps.memory_tip: Two unknowns need two relations. The sum gives α + β = 1, the product gives αβ = −6.
lines: Sum S₁ = −a₁/a₀ = 2: α + β + 1 = 2, so α + β = 1

recall.must_convey: That the sum relation gives α + β = 1 and the product relation gives αβ = −6.

steps.why: Two unknowns need two relations, and the sum and product are the two that stay simple when the third root is 1. They give α + β and αβ, which is exactly what a quadratic needs.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to subtract the known root 1 from the sum.

steps.label: Solve for α, β
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Numbers with sum 1 and product −6 are 3 and −2, the roots of y² − y − 6 = 0. Either order is correct.
steps.memory_tip: Sum 1 and product −6 are the roots of y² − y − 6 = (y − 3)(y + 2). Either order is right.

steps.why: Two numbers are fixed by their sum and product: they are the roots of y² − (sum)y + product = 0. Naming them 3 and −2 directly is fine; the quadratic is the general route when guessing fails.
common_mistakes: Giving 3 and 2 (sum 5) or −3 and 2 (sum −1) — check both sum and product.
